It was chilly and rainy this afternoon and I don't like sitting inside the house doing nothing, so Baby Ferret and I went to the mall and walked around for a while (well, I did the walking, he was in his stroller).

I needed to buy some of those little antibacterial hand gels from Bath & Body Works, so that's where I went. The place is usually a zoo, but I guess since all the teenagers were still in school at that time of day, it was dead. I grabbed a handful of the gels and went to the register to pay.

The cashier was a butter bison, probably 265 pounds if I had to guess. She immediately started cooing over my son, who was asleep in his stroller.

"Awwwwwww he's so adorable! How old is he?"

"He's 13 months," I replied.

"Awwwww so is my son! What's his name?"

I made small talk with the obeast for a few moments, and then it asked me an odd question:

"How big is he?"

"Ummmm, I don't know exactly, he's about the size of my dog," I joked uncomfortably, "so he's probably 22 or 23 pounds."

"Really? He's so tiny! My son is 35 pounds," it beamed proudly.

"He's not tiny, the doctor said he's right on target for his age," I replied sharply.

I think it knew it crossed a line. The marshmallow monster tried to backpedal. "Oh, well, my son is just bigger because he's a good eater."

"So is he," I said looking down at Baby Ferret who was still off in dreamland. "He eats everything. Broccoli, zucchini, salmon... I just discovered the other day that he really likes eggplant! He eats better than most adults I know."

Clearly I was making the gorge whore uncomfortable. Maybe she was trying to redeem the conversation and recover from the previous slight, so she forced a laugh and said, "yeah, I don't eat any of those things."

I frowned and looked at the obeast's gut pushed up against the counter, then back up at her. Stonefaced, I replied, "yeah I bet you don't."

It didn't know what to say. It just stared at me for a moment, blinked, and told me to have a good day.

I left smiling. Any day I get to shame a fatty is a good day.
